notes: Identity independently verified: supplied text identifies Freezing in response to social threat: a replication, Marret K. Noordewier, Daan T. Scheepers and Leon P. Hilbert, DOI 10.1007/s00426-019-01203-4, ORIGINAL ARTICLE; published online June 2019 and Psychological Research (2020) 84:1890–1896. Complete primary-report text has abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion and references across seven page segments. No PDF path supplied; no rendering/acquisition performed. Original side is unassigned placeholder. Target numerical test remains ambiguous. Partial eta-squared is explicitly printed, not absent; no conversion performed. Final N=54 is explicitly printed, but retained only as common-model candidate for parent field-scope review. No N inferred from df and no analytic N arithmetic used. Six recruitment exclusions: two aborted, two distorted heart-rate signals, one recording error, one anticipation of sharks in the baseline movie. Separate sensitivity analyses exclude one STAI outlier or one baseline-heart-rate outlier; these are distinct model versions, not cumulative exclusions. Candidate same-test pairs, never assigned by numeric matching: entire-sample unadjusted block F(2,52)=2.10, p=.132, partial eta-squared=.08; adjusted block F(2,51)=2.80, p=.070, partial eta-squared=.10; block × STAI F(2,51)=1.79, p=.178, partial eta-squared=.07. Entire-sample contrasts angry-neutral F(1,52)=4.47, p=.039, partial eta-squared=.08; angry-happy F(1,52)=4.25, p=.044, partial eta-squared=.08.
